big: A company offers 13% on its bond, while a government bond pays 7%. Rohan is tempted. The extra 6% is not a gift. It is the price of a risk he must understand.

lines: A company bond pays more. Why not just buy that?
Because a company can fail to pay. The extra interest is what the market charges for that chance. Ratings help you judge how big the chance is.

title: Credit and liquidity
stops: A higher rating usually means a safer borrower
A high coupon always means a safe bond
Default risk is the chance a borrower fails to pay
Every bond can be sold quickly at a fair price
caps: Rating agencies give their opinion on repayment.
A high coupon often signals higher risk.
A company may miss interest or principal.
A little-traded bond may find no buyer at a fair price.

rows: An agency's opinion on how likely repayment is
The chance that a borrower fails to pay
A bond from a company, paying more than a government bond
Difficulty selling quickly at a fair price
note: A rating is an opinion and can change. It is not a promise.

q: Two bonds: one rated high, one rated low. Which usually pays a higher coupon?
opts: The high-rated bond, since it is safer
The low-rated bond, for taking more risk
why: A safer borrower can afford to pay less, so the coupon is lower.
Coupons differ, as they reflect risk and other terms.
Both bonds pay a coupon, and the amounts differ.
A riskier borrower has to offer more to attract lenders.

q: A company misses an interest payment on its bond. What is this called?
why: A renewal is continuing a policy for another term.
Failing to pay interest or principal on time is a default.
A split is a share corporate action and not a missed payment.
A bonus issue gives extra shares and has no link to missed interest.

q: Meena holds a little-traded bond and needs cash next week. What is the risk?
opts: The bond becomes a share by itself
The coupon doubles on her need
She may not find a fair buyer
why: A bond does not turn into a share by itself.
Coupons are fixed and do not double when she needs cash.
Liquidity risk means selling quickly may be hard or costly.
That is not what liquidity risk means, since it is about selling.

q: Rohan sees a bond offering 15% from a firm with a low rating. What should he conclude?
opts: The high coupon reflects high risk
It will certainly be repaid early
why: A very high coupon on a low rating signals a higher chance of default.
A high coupon is not proof of safety. It often warns of risk.
SEBI regulates markets but does not guarantee a bond.
Nothing suggests early repayment. A riskier bond is not more certain.

pts: A higher coupon usually means higher risk.
A rating is an opinion on repayment, not a promise.
Liquidity risk: you may not sell quickly at a fair price.
